newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Berisha casts doubt on June election date - report.
newsitem.headline: Berisha casts doubt on June election date - report.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha was quoted on Thursday as saying he could not be certain that parliamentary elections in the crisis-torn Balkan state would go ahead as planned in June.
"We have set the election date for June. But at the moment there is no real progress because the (rebel) committees are still functioning," Berisha told the Austrian daily Die Presse in an interview.

Violence spread across Albania at the beginning of the year when a string of fraudulent pyramid investment schemes went under, taking with them the savings of thousands of ordinary people. Many blamed Berisha and his right-wing Democratic Party for allowing the schemes to flourish.

Insurgents, armed with weapons looted from military barracks, have seized control of much of the south and set up 'rebel committees' in some strongholds. They are refusing to hand back their guns until Berisha resigns -- something he refuses to do.
"I am a freely elected president and the silent majority supports me," Berisha told Die Presse.

He criticised former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, special envoy to Albania for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), for making contact with his opponents in the south during a recent visit.

"One should always know to whom one is talking and who they represent. There were representatives of the pyramids, leftist extremists and mafia people. I believe he should not have met them," Berisha said.
He welcomed plans for an Italian-led security force in Albania and sought to reassure the nations involved that the risks were minimal.
"Certainly there is a risk but it is not very high. Even military manoeuvres at home can present a risk to soldiers," he said.
